idea.title: Long dragons don't step into a shorter enemy head's sprint reach when a safe move exists (blunder finder's top group)
idea.hypothesis: tools/blunders.py (replays every move of ours against its alternatives for 2 turns, others' moves as recorded) finds the same largest regret group in every set it was run on: our dragon steps toward a strictly shorter enemy head 2 tiles away, which sprints in and takes a head-on that kills both, trading our length for theirs, while another move would have survived. E0065's lost games: the biggest bucket, about 1,050 regret over 240 moves; online 5409 (v0019) likewise, e.g. game 191133 r472, our 50-long dragon died trading with a 3-long. It matches M8 (most online losses end on longest). E0061's soft keep-away (-0.6, H0) paid 400 per step toward any shorter head within 5; E0032/E0047's sprint guards over-marked until every move was risky. This one is narrow: for our dragons of length >= a switchable threshold, mark only the tiles an enemy head strictly shorter than us can actually reach this turn with the sprint its length allows, and treat them as unsafe only when at least one unmarked move exists (never mark every move), behind its own switch. Measure first and after with blunders.py on the same replays: the regret and count of that group, and that no new group grows.

idea.title: Sprint-reach guard only where length decides the game: from the king beacon round, for our long dragons
idea.hypothesis: E0075's guard (P.sprintReachGuard: a dragon of length >= 5 avoids tiles a strictly shorter visible enemy head can sprint onto this turn, only while an unmarked steady move exists) worked as built: on 12 games each vs the gauntlet rammer/swarm, the blunder group 'died, shorter enemy head 2-3 away' fell from 1233 to 679 and from 1235 to 577 regret. In the SPRT's 26 lost games vs the champion, our length >= 10 dragons suffered 323 head-ons from shorter heads against the champion's 544. It still scored 0.478 vs the champion and exactly 0.50 vs swarm and rammer (-5 Elo, H0). Pearl regret rose 150-250 per 12 games, all mid-game. In the lost champion games the candidate ate 7% fewer mid and late pearls. The guard fired where it costs growth and saves little: a logging copy showed 83% of firing turns before r410 and 55% on length 5-9 dragons. Those trades drop 3-5 pearls, often into our own swarm. Build: add P.sprintGuardFromRound (default P.beaconRound, 410) so Safety::prepare sets sprintGuard only from that round, and add P.sprintGuardMinLength 10. From r410 the fold gathers mass into the king and folders, and the longest dragon decides about 55% of games at r500 (M8; online game 191133 r472: our 50-long died trading with a 3-long). Keep markSprintReach unchanged, including pearl payback and the full budget for heads whose chain runs out of sight. Tests: at r409 a 20-long dragon still eats the pearl two sprint steps from a length-4 head, and at r410 it leaves it; a length-9 dragon at r450 keeps eating; the no-escape case still moves. Measure the r410+ blunder group and our longest at r499 vs swarm and the champion before and after; the SPRT rotation's swarm score matters most.
